children.name: Auth / 9 Sync states and sign out
Note
children.text: The app always works offline. Tasks save on this Mac first and sync when the network is back. Sync never blocks typing.

children.name: Lede
children.text: Your tasks stay in your account and on your iPhone. This Mac removes its copy until you sign in again.

children.name: Text
children.text: 3 changes have not synced yet. Connect to the internet first, or they will be lost.

children.name: Note
children.text: The warning only shows when changes are waiting to sync. Otherwise the dialog is just the question.

children.name: T
children.text: Signed out, the app shows Welcome. Both buttons open the browser.

children.name: T
children.text: The sync server’s page signs you in with Touch ID (passkey plugin) or a link sent to your email (magic link plugin).

children.name: T
children.text: The page opens productivity:// with a one-time code. The app swaps it for a session.

children.name: T
children.text: If this Mac and the account both have tasks, ask once: combine, or use the account.

children.name: T
children.text: The account row in the sidebar shows sync status and opens the account menu.

children.name: Why browser
children.text: Why the browser: passkeys inside an Electron window need a paid Apple developer certificate and associated domains. The browser already has iCloud Keychain and Touch ID, and the future iPhone app can use the same passkey natively.

children.name: Lede
children.text: We sent a sign-in link to marco@example.com. Open it on this Mac. It works once and expires in 10 minutes.

children.name: Note
children.text: Clicking the link signs you in and sends you back to the app, like Touch ID does.
